description_full: Omnicom Group Inc., together with its subsidiaries, offers advertising, marketing, and corporate communications services. It provides a range of services in the areas of media and advertising, precision marketing, public relations, healthcare, branding and retail commerce, experiential, execution, and support. The company's services include advertising, branding, content marketing, crisis communications, customer data analytics and data-driven decision making, customer relationship management, decision sciences, digital experience design, digital transformation, e-commerce optimization, entertainment marketing, experiential marketing, field marketing, healthcare marketing and communications, in-store design, investor relations, and marketing research.Its services also comprise media planning and buying, merchandising and point of sale, mobile marketing, multi-cultural marketing, organizational communications, package design, performance marketing, product placement, promotional marketing, public affairs, public relations, retail media and e-commerce, shopper marketing, structured innovation, studio production, social media and influencer marketing, and sports and event marketing. It operates in the North and Latin America, Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA), and the Asia Pacific. The company was incorporated in 1944 and is based in New York, New York.

financial_summary: Omnicom Group Inc. is a large-cap communication services business with a $25.2B market cap on $17.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years and +1% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 17% against a 7% cost of capital, a 10-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.
The business throws off $2.8B in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 12.9× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.7× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 5.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 14% over the past year excluding the latest month.

val: The stock trades 30% below its DCF fair value of $132, a meaningful margin of safety.

Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 11.1% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 1.3% (vs the 8% bar).

prof: ROIC of 17% clears the cost of capital of 7.1% by 10pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.39).

Earnings quality is a concern: a weak Piotroski score of 3/9.

hlth: Leverage is heavy at 12.9x net debt to EBITDA ($3.8B of cash against $9.3B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 1.7x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.93 in the distress zone.
The current ratio of 0.93 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 6.5% over 3 years, 5.6% over 5 years and 1.3% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 11.1% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a backlog worth 3% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 29%.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (0.9% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 21, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.9%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 5.0% a year to shareholders (2.8% in buybacks and 3.5% in dividends).
The share count has grown 7.8% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It pays out 323% of earnings, more than it earns, so the dividend is at risk.
people: With about 120,000 employees, each generates about $144K of revenue, 0.2x the Communication Services median, and revenue has grown 2.5% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $23K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $586K (4x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (10/10, lower is better).
